## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The PM operations are defined in **`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`**. The system-sleep callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend()` are:

```text
PCI PM .suspend
    └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)
        └── i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
            └── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)

PCI PM .freeze
    └── i915_pm_freeze(dev)
        └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)
            └── i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
                └── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)

PCI PM .poweroff
    └── i915_pm_poweroff(dev)
        └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)
            └── i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
                └── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

The corresponding resume-side wrappers are separate paths:

```text
.resume   → i915_pm_resume()
.thaw     → i915_pm_thaw()
.restore  → i915_pm_restore()
```

They do not reach `i915_pm_suspend()`.

### Runtime PM callback

The runtime callback is a separate operation:

```text
PCI PM .runtime_suspend
    └── i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev)
        └── runtime/GEM/display runtime-PM suspend operations
```

It does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the callers that reach `i915_pm_suspend()` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()`.

| Callback/caller | Reaches `i915_pm_suspend()` | Calls `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `i915_pm_suspend()` / `.suspend` | Yes | No |
| `i915_pm_freeze()` / `.freeze` | Yes, through `i915_pm_suspend()` | No |
| `i915_pm_poweroff()` / `.poweroff` | Yes, through `i915_pm_suspend()` | No |
| `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` / `.runtime_suspend` | No | It is the callback itself |

Thus, system sleep and runtime suspend are disjoint PM paths here.

## `dev_priv` data flow

The system PM callback receives a generic `struct device *`; the i915 private state is recovered from that device and passed unchanged through the suspend helpers:

```text
struct device *kdev
    │
    │  i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
    │
    ├── dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
    │       or equivalent i915 device-to-private conversion
    │
    ▼
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
    │
    │  i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
    │
    ├── suspend GEM/GT and other driver state
    │
    └── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

There is no reallocation or transformation of the object: `dev_priv` is the same `struct drm_i915_private *` obtained from the PCI device’s driver data and passed as the argument to both `i915_drm_suspend()` and `intel_display_suspend()`.
